newsitem.title: MEXICO: No risk of Mexico devaluation - business leader.
newsitem.headline: No risk of Mexico devaluation - business leader.

text.p: The head of Mexico's top business group Hector Larios Santillan ruled out Wednesday any risk of a new devaluation in Mexico.

"No, absolutely not", he told reporters. "Here what we need to be watching is solely and exclusively that our currency has the balance and the competitivity which is needed so that (other countries') products don't end up being cheaper abroad than what we are exporting."

Larios, president of the Business Coordinating Council, was speaking after Massachusetts Institute of Technology economics guru Rudiger Dornbusch caused a stir here by saying that Mexico did not have a truly free-floating peso because Banco de Mexico was intervening to stop it from moving.

Larios said business leaders were sure that the central bank was not intervening. "I repeat, what we need to is to ensure that our currency is competitive. The president himself has committed himself to not letting our currency overvalue and this is very important," he said.

Larios said he believed predictions that the peso would be around eight to the dollar by the year end, a level which he said would "cover perfectly the undervaluation which is needed for the currency to be competitive."
